newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN cut off from 600,000 refugees in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: UN cut off from 600,000 refugees in east Zaire.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday it was cut off from nearly 600,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fleeing fighting between Tutsi rebels and troops in eastern Zaire and warned that food supplies were running out.
Spokeswoman Ruth Marshall also called for a political solution to the crisis and urged governments in the region to tackle the problems before they get out of control.
"The situation in eastern Zaire is now desperate. UNHCR is cut off from all but 400,000 of the one million refugees in eastern Zaire," Marshall told a Geneva briefing.
She said food stocks in Goma region were enough for less than a week following the looting of a U.N. food warehouse at the weekend.
Some 300,000 refugees in eastern Zaire's Uvira and Bukavu region are on the road fleeing fighting between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels.

Marshall said the only refugees UNHCR had direct access to were in Lac Vert and Mugunga camps in Goma region whose population has swollen after the arrival of nearly 200,000 Rwandan Hutus who fled a weekend attack on nearby Kibumba camp.
These two camps, where UNHCR started food distribution on Tuesday, sheltered around 400,000 people, including 10,000 displaced Zairean villagers, she said.

"We're basically distributuing all the food we have, which is good for something less than one week. We need to get the food to these people in case the mayhem in eastern zaire spreads to their area," Marshall said.
In Katale and Kahindo camps north of Goma, home to around 315,000 Rwandan Hutus, UNHCR had reports of fighting but had no access since the attacks at the weekend, she said.
The million Rwandan Hutus in eastern Zaire fled after Rwanda's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis in 1994 and many are afraid to go home where a Tutsi-led army holds sway.
